page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz and supports the x86_64 architecture with AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instructions. This instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It also includes 262 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate moderate performance characteristics. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the poor to weak categories. However, memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached read/write operations consistently rank in the average tier. Real-world execution tests, such as software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and Passmark database operations, also demonstrate average performance. Redis SET operations achieve 6.25 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is relatively weak at 6.32 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to poor for medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-8s_v3 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. The inclusion of local SSD storage and Premium Storage capabilities adds value for data-intensive operations. This server is best suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data buffering, and enterprise applications requiring substantial memory footprints but moderate CPU performance.
